chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Abu Ja'far Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abu al-Jawza' al-Munabbih ibn Abdullah, from al-Husayn ibn Alwan, from Amr ibn Khalid, from Zayd ibn Ali, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (peace be upon them) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

On the Day of Resurrection, the two-faced person will come with his tongue hanging out from behind his neck, and another tongue in front of him; the two tongues will burn with fire until they burn his body. Then it will be said to him: 'This is the one who had two faces and two tongues in the world; he will be known by that on the Day of Resurrection.'
ai.seo_question: What is the physical sign of a two-faced person on the Day of Resurrection according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq uses this hadith to illustrate the physical manifestation of *riya* (showing off) and *nifaq* (hypocrisy) on the Day of Judgment, where the hypocrite's dual nature is made literal through two tongues burning in fire. This serves as a divine retribution for those who concealed their true intentions behind a facade of piety, a concept deeply rooted in Shia exegetical traditions regarding the 'two-faced' individuals mentioned in the Quran. The imagery emphasizes that the internal duality of the hypocrite will be externally visible and eternally painful, marking them as the archetypal dissembler.
